title: Day 1 Quick Workout
description: Test your knowledge on Python interpreters, interactive mode, data types, and variable naming rules.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between the Python Interpreter and Interactive Mode?
options: Interactive mode is only for advanced users.
The Interpreter executes code, while Interactive Mode is a way of interacting with the interpreter line-by-line.
Interactive mode can only execute .py files.
There is no difference, they are exactly the same.
questions.explanation: The interpreter is the program that actually executes the code. Interactive mode (REPL) is an interface where you type code one line at a time and see the result immediately.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct data type for the value: 25.5?
questions.explanation: A float represents a number containing a decimal value.

questions.question:
What will be the output of the following code?

print("20" + "10")
questions.explanation: Because 20 and 10 are inside quotes, Python treats them as strings (text). The '+' operator joins the two strings together instead of doing math.

questions.question: Which of the following is an INVALID variable name in Python?
questions.explanation: Rule 1: A variable cannot start with a number. Therefore, '1student' is invalid.

questions.question: How do you properly declare a boolean value in Python?
questions.explanation: Boolean values in Python must be capitalized: True or False.
